title: Elasticity Gardener: Budget tiller and hiring heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is an experimental, operational budgeting "tiller" — a compact workbook + playbook for running short (6–18 week) headcount phasing and pricing-sensitivity experiments. The goal is to keep a live, small-footprint decision artifact finance can iterate with product and serving to:
- buy runway when price elasticity is favorable,
- protect SLAs with sprint reserves when demand is uncertain, and
- show step-by-step hiring gates tied to pricing triggers rather than big monolithic hiring plans.

Key idea (Gardener metaphor):
Treat the budget like a garden bed you tend weekly: small, local tilts (price promos, reserve pools, short-term contractors) rather than wholesale replanting. Each tilt has measurable yield (tokens/month, customer retention uplift, committed revenue) and an operational cost (GPU spend, support headcount).

Summary of scenarios (6-month rolling window):
- Baseline (steady growth): price unchanged, uptake +10% QoQ, conservative hiring for attrition + small growth.
- Tight lane (price pressure): market price compression -15% leads to demand elasticity +35% in token volume but lower revenue per token; use reserve buckets and deferred perm hiring.
- Capture push (aggressive discount): temporary -30% price to win ARR from targeted accounts; requires temporary surge capacity and sales engineering support; expect 2–3x short-term token spike.
- Cost-first (quantization + cadence): adopt aggressive quantization and batching, reduce per-token cost by ~18%, use savings to fund 6-week hiring experiment for serving runtime.

Headcount phasing table (high level, by functional band — numbers are FTE equivalents and contract pools):
CSV: role,baseline_add_q2,baseline_add_q3,tightlane_min_pool,capture_surge_pool
SRE,1,1,0.5,1.5
Serving-Engineers,2,3,1.0,4.0
-Applied-ML,1,1,0.5,1.0
-Product-Manager,0.25,0.25,0,0.5
-Sales-Eng,0.5,0.5,0,2.0
-Customer-Success,0.5,0.5,0.25,1.0

Assumptions behind numbers:
- Baseline hiring is intentionally modest; Q2 adds assume we convert 50% of open requisitions to perm hires, rest to contractors.
- Tight lane keeps minimal perm hires and fills capacity with contractors and overtime where feasible.
- Capture surge uses a 12-week contractor pool and pre-bought GPU credits (reserve bucket) to avoid long-term payroll commitment.

Reserve buckets and financial treatment:
- GPU reserve bucket: prebooked credits representing 8–12 weeks of moderate surge capacity. Capitalize as prepaid cost and amortize against the period when used; treat as contingent cost in the base forecast.
- Contractor pool: funded as Opex buffer; toggled on/off by SRE/Eng lead with 2-week notice.
- Coupon/discount budget: allocated from marketing and revenue acceleration line; tracked to ARR acquired (convert rate) for ROI.

Pricing-sensitivity matrix (quick lookup):
- Price change -> demand multiplier -> gross unit-revenue change -> headcount delta (net)
Examples (model inputs used in the sheet):
- -25% price -> demand x1.8 -> revenue per token down 25% but gross revenue change = -25%*x1.8 = +35% net (so revenue may actually increase if demand elastic enough) -> requires +30–60% servicing capacity (SRE + serving-engineers), partial offset by batching gains.
- +10% price -> demand x0.85 -> revenue per token up 10% but token volume falls; net revenue ~ -5% — allows hiring pause and reallocation to product.

Trigger rules (executable):
1) If realized token volume > modelled baseline by +40% for 2 consecutive weeks AND gross margin per token < baseline by >8%, open Surge Protocol: prepay GPU bucket, spin up contractor pool, cap new perm hires for 6 weeks.
2) If monthly ARR uplift from coupon channel < target conversion (3% of engaged leads) after 8 weeks, stop coupon and reallocate funds to retention engineering.
3) If batching/quantization experiments achieve >15% per-token cost reduction within a full test cohort (n>=10k tokens) then accelerate reallocation of 50% savings to perm hires in Serving (up to 3 hires).

Monitoring signals (what finance needs to watch weekly):
- tokens per minute (TPM) and 90/99 latency SLA — correlate with running GPU utilization; if TPU>80% and latency drift, fire Surge Protocol.
- effective revenue per token, by customer cohort and route — watch for cohort-level elasticity differences.
- contractor burn vs. recruit ramp — if contractor spend > planned by 20% with <1% conversion to perm we pivot to frozen hiring.

Short experiments (playbook):
Experiment A — "Coupon gardener": 6-week targeted discount for developer community cohort (selected by usage pattern). Budget: $120k coupon allocation, expected ARR capture $300k NRR over 12 months. Operational needs: 0.6 FE Sales-Eng, 1 contractor Support for 8 weeks, prebooked 25% surge GPU credits. KPI: conversion to paid within 30 days, support tickets per 1k calls.

Experiment B — "Batch-first": 8-week rollout of automatic aggressive batching on a 5% traffic shadow. Budget delta: expected -18% per-token cost. Quick-stop rule: if error rates or latency regress >2x baseline, revert and perform root cause.

Sensitivity visualization notes (how the sheet is structured):
- Left pane: knobs (price delta slider, conversion rates, contractor-to-perm conversion, quantization savings).
- Center pane: scenario outputs (revenue by month, headcount by role, opex/capex buckets, runway impact).
- Right pane: waterfall view (impact of each toggle on monthly cashflow and runway days).

Recommended next steps for review meeting (finance + eng + product):
- Validate elasticity priors for top 10 customers (ask Sales/Account to provide observed price tensions).
- Approve $250k for initial coupon and reserve buckets (split CAPEX/OPEX as suggested).
- Trial Batch-first experiment in a green environment for 6 weeks with weekly readouts.
- Assign owners: Miguel Ortega (SRE lead) for Surge Protocol, Priya Desai (Product Finance) for coupon ROI tracking, Ethan Park (Talent ops) to build contractor-to-perm tracker.

Open questions and risks:
- Elasticity is cohort-specific; a single global model overweights heavy users. We need to estimate elasticity by top-20 customers separately.
- Contractor conversion risk: if we rely heavily on contractors to absorb tight-lane demand, conversion costs and knowledge transfer may erode expected savings.
- Regulatory / enterprise procurement obligations could prevent rapid discounting for target accounts; Legal needs to vet capture playbook.

Appendices included in the sheet (tabs):
- assumptions: list of model inputs and priors used for each scenario (percent ranges).
- role-costing: fully-burdened cost per FTE by role (salary + benefits + recruiting amortized).
- GPU-cost-sim: discrete scenarios of spot vs. reserved pricing and amortization schedule.
- cohort-elasticity: raw sales feedback and observed usage deltas (placeholder table).

Notes to reviewer (quick):
- This is a working prototype (sheet + short playbook). Numbers are intentionally conservative on perm hires and optimistic on contractor availability. Please flag any role-cost inputs that look off for your team.
- If approved for pilot funding, we will run the 6–12 week experiments and reconvene to convert successful short-term capacity into longer-term hiring decisions.
